scenes.heading: Congruent figures
scenes.sub: Exact copies, matched part by part
scenes.say: Tiles, car parts and copied keys all need to be exact copies, or they won't fit. In maths, exact copies are called congruent. Let's learn how to name them and use them to find missing sides and angles.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A copied key matches the original in every notch
scenes.science: Congruent figures match in every side and angle
scenes.breaks: A flipped key may not fit the lock, but a flipped (reflected) shape still counts as congruent.
scenes.say: A copied house key must match the original exactly, every notch and every edge. Congruent shapes are the same: one fits exactly on top of the other. One difference: a flipped key might not fit the lock, but a flipped shape still counts as congruent.

scenes.heading: What congruent means
points: Matching sides and angles are equal
Same area alone is NOT enough
scenes.say: Congruent means same size and same shape. All matching sides and matching angles are equal, so the perimeters and areas are equal too. But careful: two shapes with the same area aren't always congruent. A two by twelve rectangle and a four by six rectangle both have area twenty-four.

scenes.heading: The congruence statement
scenes.say: We write triangle A B C is congruent to triangle P Q R using this symbol. The order of the letters matters. A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R. So side B C matches side Q R.

scenes.heading: Use the marks to match the parts
notes: Same number of dashes: matching sides
Same number of arcs: matching angles
A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R
scenes.say: Here are two congruent triangles, one flipped over. First the triangles, then the marks. One dash matches one dash, two dashes match two, and arcs work the same way for angles. So A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R.

scenes.heading: Finding an unknown angle
scenes.question: ABCD ≅ EFGH. ∠A = 80°, ∠B = 95°, ∠C = 110°. Find ∠H.
scenes.say: A B C D is congruent to E F G H. Find angle H. H is the fourth letter, so it matches D. The angles of a quadrilateral add to three hundred and sixty. Three sixty minus eighty, ninety-five and one hundred and ten leaves seventy-five. So angle H is seventy-five degrees.
scenes.caption: ABCD ≅ EFGH. H is the 4th letter, so ∠H = ∠D. Angles add to 360°: 360° − (80° + 95° + 110°) = 75°. So ∠H = 75°.

scenes.heading: Using algebra
scenes.question: △ABC ≅ △DEF. AB = 3y − 2 and DE = y + 8. Find AB.
scenes.say: A B matches D E, so set them equal: three y minus two equals y plus eight. Take y from both sides and add two: two y equals ten, so y is five. Substitute: A B is three times five minus two, which is thirteen centimetres. Check: D E is five plus eight, also thirteen.
scenes.caption: AB matches DE, so 3y − 2 = y + 8. Then 2y = 10, so y = 5. AB = 3 × 5 − 2 = 13 cm. Check: DE = 5 + 8 = 13 ✓

scenes.say: Quick recap. Congruent means same size and same shape, even if one is flipped or turned. The order of letters in the statement shows which parts match. Matching sides and angles are equal. And same area alone isn't enough. Now try the practice questions!
